Script.name: clanshops
Script.script:
if not (aardkit and aardkit.util and aardkit.register) then if cecho then cecho("\n<firebrick>[Clan Shops]<reset> needs Aardkit Core. Install that first - Toolbox > Module Manager, priority 1.\n") end return end
--[[ Clan Shops — the clan shop rooms, and what's in them Sean Stoves, 2026-08-02
The stock module has this as a hover menu called ClanShops: sixty room ids grouped into submenus by area, each entry calling gotoRoom(). That function is called seventeen times in that module and defined nowhere in it - not as a function, not as an assignment, not as aard.gotoRoom - so every entry, and every 'runto' link in its room-find output, calls a nil global. It has been dead for some time and nothing about our mapper caused it.
The list of rooms is worth keeping. It's a fact about Aardwolf rather than anyone's code, and sixty room numbers are not something to rediscover by walking. So: the same rooms, in a table you can read, with a [go] on each that goes through our own walker.
Better with Loot Tracker, and useless-but-harmless without it. That module already records shop_stock keyed by roomid - what a shop natively stocks and asks for it - which is exactly the join this needs. With it installed you can search every clan shop for an item without visiting one. ]]
aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.clanshops = aardkit.clanshops or {}
local CS = aardkit.clanshops local U = aardkit.util.named("Clan Shops")
--- -- the rooms -- -- Read out of the stock module's own list, which is where anyone would have -- had to get them. Room numbers and clan names are facts about the MUD. ---
local SHOPS = { { 30525, "bard" }, { 30531, "bard" }, { 30532, "bard" }, { 30533, "bard" }, { 49256, "boot" }, { 49392, "boot" }, { 50102, "boot" }, { 50103, "boot" }, { 31123, "crusader" }, { 49217, "crusader" }, { 47187, "crusader" }, { 31150, "crusader" }, { 31158, "crusader" }, { 31128, "crusader" }, { 31156, "crusader" }, { 49335, "gaardian" }, { 20029, "gaardian" }, { 20035, "gaardian" }, { 14162, "seekers" }, { 14141, "seekers" }, { 14168, "seekers" }, { 31594, "tanelorn" }, { 31584, "tanelorn" }, { 31566, "tanelorn" }, { 29214, "tao" }, { 29220, "tao" }, { 29221, "tao" }, { 29223, "tao" }, { 49373, "tao" }, { 50152, "touchstone" }, { 28358, "touchstone" },{ 28361, "touchstone" },{ 28359, "touchstone" }, { 50123, "touchstone" },{ 34210, "amazon" }, { 15704, "cabal" }, { 28910, "chaos" }, { 27991, "crimson" }, { 30949, "daoine" }, { 16803, "doh" }, { 5865, "dominion" }, { 642, "dragon" }, { 29580, "druid" }, { 831, "emerald" }, { 2292, "hook" }, { 30415, "imperium" }, { 2339, "light" }, { 28580, "loqui" }, { 15855, "masaki" }, { 19967, "perdition" }, { 15141, "pyre" }, { 1961, "retribution" },{ 502, "rhabdo" }, { 24182, "romani" }, { 32408, "shadokil" }, { 15574, "twinlobe" }, { 879, "vanir" }, { 32342, "watchmen" }, { 49572, "xunti" }, }
local by_room = {} for _, r in ipairs(SHOPS) do by_room[r[1]] = r[2] end
--- -- stock -- -- Loot Tracker owns this when it's installed. It records shop_stock keyed by -- roomid already, for every shop on Aardwolf rather than these sixty, and two -- modules writing the same fact is how they drift apart - so when it's here we -- read its table and record nothing ourselves. -- -- When it isn't, this keeps its own, from the same 'list' output and the same -- trigger pattern it uses. Only for the sixty rooms above: this is a clan shop -- command and has no business remembering the whole game. ---
local STOCK = U.load("clanshops", { stock = {} }) STOCK.stock = STOCK.stock or {}
local function ours_saves() return not U.have("loot") end
-- Only ever this module's own table, whoever is in charge of reading. The -- ownership rule is "we don't write when Loot Tracker is here", and that is -- invisible through stock_of, which reads theirs in that case. function CS.own_stock(id) return STOCK.stock[tostring(id)] or {} end
function CS.on_shop(lvl, price, item) if not ours_saves() then return end -- theirs is the record item = U.trim(tostring(item or "")) if item == "" then return end local id = U.room() if not (id and by_room[id]) then return end -- only clan shops
local shop = STOCK.stock[tostring(id)] or {} for _, e in ipairs(shop) do if e.item == item then e.price, e.level, e.seen = tonumber(price) or 0, tonumber(lvl) or 0, os.time() STOCK.stock[tostring(id)] = shop U.save("clanshops", STOCK) return end end shop[#shop + 1] = { item = item, price = tonumber(price) or 0, level = tonumber(lvl) or 0, seen = os.time() } STOCK.stock[tostring(id)] = shop U.save("clanshops", STOCK) end
-- Every item recorded for a room, from whichever record is in charge. -- Public because it's the only way to see which record that is - a test that -- goes through 'find' cannot tell "we didn't store it" from "we didn't read it". function CS.stock_of(id) if U.have("loot") and aardkit.loot.t and aardkit.loot.t.shop_stock then local T = aardkit.loot.t local ok, rows = pcall(function() return db:fetch(T.shop_stock, db:eq(T.shop_stock.roomid, id)) end) if ok and type(rows) == "table" then local out = {} for _, r in ipairs(rows) do out[#out + 1] = { item = tostring(r.item), price = tonumber(r.price) or 0, level = tonumber(r.level) or 0 } end return out end return {} end return STOCK.stock[tostring(id)] or {} end
local stock_of = CS.stock_of
--- -- what we can say about a room ---
local function known(id) return roomExists and roomExists(id) and true or false end
local function room_name(id) if not known(id) then return "?" end local ok, n = pcall(getRoomName, id) return (ok and n ~= "" and n) or "?" end
local function area_of(id) if not known(id) then return "?" end if aardkit.mapper and aardkit.mapper.areaname then return aardkit.mapper.areaname(id) end return "?" end
local function stocked(id) return #stock_of(id) end
local function go_link(id) -- Our walker if the Mapper is here; the MUD's own runto if it isn't. Never -- gotoRoom, which is what theirs calls and what nothing defines. if aardkit.mapper and aardkit.mapper.goto_room then return { "<#3ad07a>[go]<r>", function() aardkit.mapper.goto_room(id) end, "Walk to " .. U.rid(id) } end return { "<#3ad07a>[go]<r>", function() send("runto " .. id, false) end, "runto " .. id .. " (install the Mapper to walk it properly)" } end
--- -- listing ---
function CS.list(filter) filter = U.trim(tostring(filter or "")):lower()
local rows, unmapped = {}, 0 for _, s in ipairs(SHOPS) do local id, clan = s[1], s[2] if filter == "" or clan:find(filter, 1, true) or tostring(id) == filter or room_name(id):lower():find(filter, 1, true) then if not known(id) then unmapped = unmapped + 1 end local n = stocked(id) local row = { clan, area_of(id), room_name(id), id, n and tostring(n) or "-" } row.link = go_link(id) rows[#rows + 1] = row end end
if #rows == 0 then U.warn("No clan shop matching '" .. filter .. "'. 'clanshops' for the lot.") return end table.sort(rows, function(a, b) if a[1] ~= b[1] then return a[1] < b[1] end return a[4] < b[4] end)
local foot = #rows .. " clan shop(s)." if not U.have("loot") then foot = foot .. " 'items' is blank without Loot Tracker." end if unmapped > 0 then foot = foot .. " " .. unmapped .. " not in your map yet." end
U.table({ { "clan", max = 12 }, { "area", max = 22 }, { "room", flex = true }, { "rm uid", align = "r" }, { "items", align = "r" }, }, rows, foot) end
-- Every clan shop that stocks something matching, which is the thing their -- hover menu could never answer: it knew where the shops were and nothing -- about what was in them. function CS.find(text) text = U.trim(tostring(text or "")):lower() if text == "" then U.warn("Usage: clanshops find <item>"); return end
local out = {} for _, sh in ipairs(SHOPS) do local id, clan = sh[1], sh[2] for _, e in ipairs(stock_of(id)) do if e.item:lower():find(text, 1, true) then local row = { clan, e.item, e.level, e.price, id } row.link = go_link(id) out[#out + 1] = row end end end
if #out == 0 then U.note("Nothing matching '" .. text .. "' recorded in a clan shop yet.") if ours_saves() then U.note("Stock is learned by running 'list' in one - " .. CS.seen_count() .. " of " .. #SHOPS .. " visited so far.") U.suggest("loot", "Loot Tracker records every shop on Aardwolf, not just these") else U.note("'loot shop " .. text .. "' searches every shop, not only clan ones.") end return end table.sort(out, function(a, b) return a[4] < b[4] end)
U.table({ { "clan", max = 12 }, { "item", flex = true }, { "level", align = "r" }, { "price", align = "r" }, { "rm uid", align = "r" }, }, out, #out .. " match(es), cheapest first.") end
-- how many of the sixty we have any stock for function CS.seen_count() local n = 0 for _, sh in ipairs(SHOPS) do if #stock_of(sh[1]) > 0 then n = n + 1 end end return n end
--- -- commands ---
function CS.cmd(arg) local verb, rest = U.split_verb(arg) rest = U.trim(rest)
if verb == "find" or verb == "item" then CS.find(rest)
elseif verb == "forget" then if not ours_saves() then U.note("Loot Tracker owns the stock record - 'loot clear shop' is the one that clears it.") return end STOCK.stock = {} U.save("clanshops", STOCK) U.ok("Forgot what this module had learned about clan shop stock.")
elseif verb == "help" then U.help("Clan Shops", { { "shops", #SHOPS .. " rooms" }, { "stock", U.have("loot") and "Loot Tracker's, for every shop on Aardwolf" or ("ours, learned from 'list' - " .. CS.seen_count() .. " of " .. #SHOPS .. " visited") }, { "" }, { "clanshops", "all of them, with a [go] on each" }, { "clanshops <clan>", "one clan - 'clanshops tao'" }, { "clanshops find <item>", "which clan shop stocks it" }, { "clanshops forget", "drop the stock this module learned" }, { "" }, { "The room list is the stock module's own. Its ClanShops menu walks" }, { "you there with gotoRoom(), which that module calls seventeen times" }, { "and defines nowhere - so those entries have been dead a while." }, })
else CS.list(arg) end end
aardkit.register("clanshops", "clan shop rooms, and what's in them", CS.cmd)
